verses.sanskrit:
तपःस्वाध्यायनिरतं तपस्वी वाग्विदां वरम् ।
नारदं परिपप्रच्छ वाल्मीकिर्मुनिपुङ्गवम् ॥
verses.translation: The ascetic Valmiki, ever devoted to penance and study, asked the celestial sage Narada, foremost among the eloquent and best among sages.

verses.sanskrit:
को न्वस्मिन् साम्प्रतं लोके गुणवान् कश्च वीर्यवान् ।
धर्मज्ञश्च कृतज्ञश्च सत्यवाक्यो दृढव्रतः ॥
verses.translation: Who in this world today is virtuous? Who is valiant? Who is righteous, grateful, truthful, and firm in his vows?

verses.sanskrit:
चारित्रेण च को युक्तः सर्वभूतेषु को हितः ।
विद्वान् कः कश्च समर्थश्च कश्चैकप्रियदर्शनः ॥
verses.translation: Who is endowed with good character? Who is well-disposed to all beings? Who is learned and capable, and who is ever pleasant to behold?

verses.sanskrit:
इक्ष्वाकुवंशप्रभवो रामो नाम जनैः श्रुतः ।
नियतात्मा महावीर्यो द्युतिमान् धृतिमान् वशी ॥
verses.translation: Born in the Ikshvaku dynasty, known to the people as Rama — self-controlled, mighty in valor, radiant, steadfast, and master of his senses.

verses.sanskrit:
विश्वामित्रस्तदा वाक्यमश्रृण्वन् राघवो वचः ।
वैदेहीं च महाभागो लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम् ॥
verses.translation: Then the illustrious Rama heard the words of Sage Vishvamitra, and accompanied by the blessed Sita and the mighty Lakshmana, set forth on the great journey.

chapters.title: Ayodhya Kanda — The Book of Ayodhya

verses.sanskrit:
ततः पुरुषशार्दूलः सत्यसन्धो जितेन्द्रियः ।
रामो दाशरथिः श्रीमान् नयति स्म महावशी ॥
verses.translation: Then the tiger among men, the truthful, self-controlled, glorious Rama, son of Dasharatha, the great master of his senses, departed for the forest.

verses.sanskrit:
रामः प्रव्राजितो वनम् भरतो राज्यमाप्नुयात् ।
इत्येवं दूषिता राज्ञी कैकेयी प्रविवेश ह ॥
verses.translation: That Rama should be exiled to the forest and Bharata should obtain the kingdom — thus poisoned, Queen Kaikeyi entered the chamber of wrath.

verses.sanskrit:
पितुर्वचनमाज्ञाय रामो वनमगच्छत ।
सीता लक्ष्मणसहिता धर्मं पालयतः सदा ॥
verses.translation: Obeying his father's command, Rama went to the forest, accompanied by Sita and Lakshmana, ever upholding dharma.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रविश्य तु महारण्यं रामो राजीवलोचनः ।
विराधं राक्षसं घोरं जजान सहलक्ष्मणः ॥
verses.translation: Entering the great forest, the lotus-eyed Rama, together with Lakshmana, slew the fierce demon Viradha.

verses.sanskrit:
खरदूषणमुख्यांश्च राक्षसान् चतुर्दश सहस्राणि ।
जघान रणमूर्धनि रामो दशरथात्मजः ॥
verses.translation: Rama, son of Dasharatha, slew Khara, Dushana, and their chief warriors — fourteen thousand demons — in the forefront of battle.

verses.sanskrit:
मारीचं मृगरूपेण रावणो जानकीं हरत् ।
गृध्रराजं च जटायुं हत्वा सीतां ससार ह ॥
verses.translation: Using Maricha in the form of a golden deer as a trick, Ravana abducted Janaki (Sita). After slaying the vulture king Jatayu, he carried Sita away.

chapters.title: Kishkindha Kanda — The Kingdom of Monkeys

verses.sanskrit:
ततो वानरराजेन सुग्रीवेण समागतः ।
सख्यं च कृतवान् रामो वालिनं चैव जघ्नवान् ॥
verses.translation: Then Rama met Sugriva, the king of the monkeys, formed an alliance of friendship, and slew Vali.

verses.sanskrit:
सुग्रीवः सहितो रामं सीताम्न्वेषणमादिशत् ।
हनुमान् वायुपुत्रश्च सागरं लङ्घयत्ततः ॥
verses.translation: Sugriva, allied with Rama, ordered the search for Sita. Then Hanuman, the son of the Wind God, leapt across the ocean.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो रावणनीतायाः सीतायाः शत्रुकर्षणः ।
इयेष पदमन्विच्छन् पवनात्मजसत्तमः ॥
verses.translation: Then the most excellent son of the Wind God, the tormentor of enemies, set out to find the trail of Sita, who had been carried away by Ravana.

verses.sanskrit:
स सागरमनाधृष्यं शतयोजनमायतम् ।
अतिक्रम्य महातेजा हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः ॥
verses.translation: The mighty Hanuman, son of the Wind God, crossed the impassable ocean stretching a hundred yojanas wide.

verses.sanskrit:
लङ्कायां दृष्ट्वा वैदेहीं ध्यायन्तीं राममव्ययम् ।
सम्प्रत्ययमुपागम्य सूचयामास मैथिलीम् ॥
verses.translation: In Lanka, he found Vaidehi (Sita) meditating on the imperishable Rama. Gaining her trust, he identified himself to the princess of Mithila.

verses.sanskrit:
अशोकवनिकायां तां दृष्ट्वा रामप्रियां प्रभुः ।
मुद्रिकां राघवस्यैव सम्प्रदर्श्य ततः कपिः ॥
verses.translation: In the Ashoka grove, the lord of monkeys found Rama's beloved and showed her the signet ring of Raghava.

verses.sanskrit:
ततो युद्धे महाघोरे रामरावणयोर्भवत् ।
देवासुरसमं युद्धमद्भुतं लोकसाक्षिकम् ॥
verses.translation: Then a great and terrible battle occurred between Rama and Ravana — a marvelous war rivaling the battles of gods and demons, witnessed by the world.

verses.sanskrit:
रावणं निहत्य रामो लब्ध्वा सीतां यशस्विनीम् ।
पुष्पकेण विमानेन ननन्द सहलक्ष्मणः ॥
verses.translation: Having slain Ravana and won back the glorious Sita, Rama, together with Lakshmana, rejoiced in the Pushpaka aerial chariot.

verses.sanskrit:
अयोध्यां प्राप्य राजानम् अभिषिच्य यथाविधि ।
राज्यं कारयामास लोकानां हितकाम्यया ॥
verses.translation: Returning to Ayodhya and being consecrated as king according to the sacred rites, Rama ruled the kingdom for the welfare of all beings.

verses.sanskrit:
रामराज्ये जगत् सर्वं सुखिनः सर्वे जनाः ।
धर्मपालनतत्पराः सर्वे सत्यपरायणाः ॥
verses.translation: In the reign of Rama, the entire world was happy, all people were devoted to upholding dharma and committed to truth.

verses.sanskrit:
नालोक्यते जनपदे रोगिणो वा कृशः क्वचित् ।
न च स्मर्यते दुःखं राज्ये रामस्य धीमतः ॥
verses.translation: In the kingdom, there were no sick or emaciated people to be seen anywhere, and sorrow was unknown in the realm of the wise Rama.
